name: Sodium Benzoate
description: Sodium salt of benzoic acid used widely in acidic foods, carbonated beverages, jams, and condiments to inhibit mould and bacterial proliferation.
notes: Subject to maximum permitted limit controls in beverages due to potential benzene formation in the presence of ascorbic acid (Vitamin C).

name: Citric Acid
description: Naturally occurring organic tricarboxylic acid produced industrially by fermentation of carbohydrates by Aspergillus niger.
notes: Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) with widespread use in beverages, confectionery, and dairy.

name: Lecithins
description: A mixture of phospholipids extracted from plant seeds (soybeans, sunflowers) or egg yolks, enabling stable oil-in-water emulsions.
notes: May indicate the presence of soy or egg allergens depending on the botanical/biological extraction source.

name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
description: Sodium salt of glutamic acid produced via bacterial fermentation of molasses or starch, imparting the savory 'umami' taste.
notes: Scientifically evaluated as safe by WHO/FAO JECFA; individual sensitivity has been reported but not consistently replicated in double-blind trials.

name: Sodium Nitrite
description: Inorganic salt used in cured meats to prevent Clostridium botulinum growth and preserve pink meat color.
notes: Strictly regulated in meat products due to potential formation of nitrosamines at high frying temperatures.

name: Tartrazine
description: Synthetic azo dye yielding a bright lemon-yellow shade in snacks, confectionery, and soft drinks.
notes: EU requires a warning statement regarding activity and attention in children; FDA requires specific label declaration for sensitive individuals.

name: Sunset Yellow FCF
description: Synthetic petroleum-derived orange azo dye used in confectionery, desserts, and bakery goods.
notes: Requires child warning label in EU; regulated with maximum limits in India, US, and Canada.

name: Allura Red AC
description: Red azo dye used to colour sweets, sauces, cereals, and dairy desserts.
notes: Approved in USA, EU, India, UK, and Canada subject to category-specific maximum use levels.

name: Caramel IV (Sulphite Ammonia Caramel)
description: Water-soluble food colouring prepared by heat treatment of carbohydrates with ammonium and sulphite compounds; used in colas, beer, and gravies.
notes: Levels of 4-MEI byproduct are monitored and regulated under safety guidelines internationally.

name: Sorbic Acid
description: Naturally occurring and synthetically produced unsaturated fatty acid that inhibits yeasts and moulds in cheese, baked goods, and dried fruit.
notes: Metabolized similarly to natural dietary fatty acids.

name: Potassium Sorbate
description: Potassium salt of sorbic acid with high water solubility, preventing mould and yeast growth in yogurt, wine, dips, and baked products.
notes: Recognized as safe across global jurisdictions with numerical acceptable daily intakes (ADI).

name: Calcium Propionate
description: Organic salt inhibiting mould and 'rope' bacterium formation in bread and commercial bakery items.
notes: Extensively permitted internationally in bread and baked goods with GMP or established numerical limits.

name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
description: Essential water-soluble vitamin and powerful reducing agent protecting against lipid oxidation and enzymatic browning.
notes: Widespread permitted use under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP).

name: Tocopherol-rich Extract (Vitamin E)
description: Fat-soluble antioxidants extracted from vegetable oils to delay oxidative rancidity in fats and oils.
notes: Widely permitted natural antioxidant.

name: Carrageenan
description: Family of natural sulfated polysaccharides extracted from red edible seaweeds, stabilizing dairy emulsions and plant milks.
notes: Subject to strict purity criteria specifying low degraded carrageenan (poligeenan) fractions.

name: Guar Gum
description: Galactomannan polysaccharide extracted from the endosperm of the guar bean (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba).
notes: Natural dietary soluble fiber widely permitted under GMP.

name: Xanthan Gum
description: High-molecular-weight polysaccharide produced by fermentation of glucose or sucrose by Xanthomonas campestris.
notes: Highly effective pseudoplastic rheology modifier used in salad dressings, sauces, and gluten-free baking.

name: Diphosphates
description: Salts of pyrophosphoric acid functioning as leavening acids in baking powder and moisture retainers in processed meats.
notes: Total dietary phosphorus intake monitored by regulatory agencies.

name: Mono- and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
description: Non-ionic emulsifiers synthesized from glycerol and natural plant or animal fatty acids, retarding bread staling and stabilizing margarine.
dietary: Vegetarian if certified vegetable oil origin; non-vegetarian if derived from animal tallow.
notes: Most commercial food grade E471 is derived from palm or soybean oil.

name: Sodium Carbonates (Baking Soda)
description: Mineral salts releasing carbon dioxide upon heating or acid reaction, creating light airy texture in biscuits and cakes.
notes: Traditional leavening agent with broad global GMP approvals.

name: Ammonium Carbonates
description: Leavening salt releasing ammonia and carbon dioxide during high-temperature baking; evaporates completely leaving no residual moisture.
notes: Used principally in dry crispy crackers and cookies.

name: Acesulfame Potassium (Ace-K)
description: Calorie-free sugar substitute approximately 200 times sweeter than sucrose with high thermal stability.
notes: Permitted with defined ADI (typically 9-15 mg/kg body weight depending on jurisdiction).

name: Aspartame
description: Low-calorie artificial dipeptide sweetener (aspartic acid and phenylalanine) providing intense sweetness.
notes: Mandatory warning label required for individuals with Phenylketonuria (PKU): 'Contains Phenylalanine'.

name: Sucralose
description: Zero-calorie high-intensity organochlorine sweetener approximately 600 times sweeter than table sugar, stable across heat and diverse pH ranges.
notes: Extensively approved across FDA, EFSA, FSSAI, Health Canada, and FSA.

name: Steviol Glycosides (Stevia)
description: High-intensity natural non-nutritive glycosides extracted and purified from the leaves of Stevia rebaudiana.
notes: Global regulatory approval as non-caloric botanical sweetener.
